pat_manchester.text: Manchester branch. Open till half past four, and not a minute after. The rain doesn't count as an excuse, though I've tried.
Mind how you go, love. And keep a little back for the bus.

saver_manchester.text: I've put a fiver in every Friday since I started work. It's not much. It's mine, and it's here.

then.text: I've deleted it. Forwarded it, too. Feels oddly satisfying.

else.text: Look at this, would you. 'Pat's Building Society: your account is LOCKED. Confirm your details within 2 hours at pats-secure-login.link or lose access.'
It's from a number I don't know. I've two hours. Is it real?

options: Delete it and forward it to 7726
Ring the number it came from

then.text: Oh no. That is exactly what they hoped for. If you ever do, ring your bank on the number on your card straight away, and change the password.
Good. 7726 spells SPAM on the keypad, if that helps you remember. It's free, and your mobile provider looks into the sender.
Ringing the number in the message only gets you the scammer. Always use a number you already trust.

else.text: Three giveaways. It rushes you, it comes from a number that isn't the society's, and the link isn't their real address.
A real society won't text you a login link, and nobody genuine will ever ask for the code they send you. Not staff, not the police, not 'the fraud team'.
Emails work the same way. Forward the dodgy ones to report@phishing.gov.uk and don't click anything. If in doubt, ring the number on the back of your card.
Here, have this. My daughter makes them and I can't be trusted with the tin.
Noted in the Almanac under Things worth knowing.
